product: personal AI task planner (first PEOS proof)
authority: Product decisions belong exclusively to the owner or a product manager he explicitly authorizes. An unanswered decision is not a fallback value.

D1.question: What must PEOS deliver first?
D1.answer: A complete AI task planner with a UI on localhost; PEOS performs architecture, engineering, AI, testing and local delivery using reusable components/templates.

D2.question: For fresh generation (G4), is the trusted-operator model sufficient when an actual session's request/response evidence is independently retained, or is stronger provider-authenticated proof required?

D3.question: Should G2 prove the verifier rejects frozen known-bad fixtures, or that it detects defects injected into each newly generated candidate?

D4.question: Monitoring system of record: pm-evals-web, obsplane, or defer the choice?
D4.notes: Does not block PEOS repair or the planner.

D5.question: Outcome metric and target, leading metrics, guardrails and main trade-off: what must the user accomplish, with what limits on manual effort, time and errors?

D6.question: Who uses it and how is it distributed?
D6.answer: One person locally; others fork the PEOS workflow/repository and run their own instance. No tenancy or shared hosting.

D7.question: UI behaviour and template inputs: screens, journeys, and the clickable approval pop-up surface (local web UI notification vs OS-native).

D8.question: Must the product itself contain AI?
D8.answer: Yes: an automatic task builder that interprets work conversations; AI-assisted coding alone does not satisfy it.

D9.question: Which conversation sources?
D9.answer: ChatGPT is required and primary; Claude is optional and may be omitted if it adds substantial complexity; requested local Wispr text and other authorized sources after access is verified.

D10.question: How are tasks derived?
D10.answer: Infer tasks from discussions and follow the latest agreed state; a later agreement (e.g. tomorrow changed to ten days later) supersedes, and quoting an old plan does not restore it. Remind before deadlines (policy in D14).

D11.question: Calendar write policy?
D11.answer: New entries are created automatically in the evening batch when information and scheduling rules are settled; changes to existing entries require approval through a clickable pop-up; reprocessing must not duplicate events.

D12b.question: Which Google calendar receives entries, and may any other people be invited (attendees / invitation emails)?

D13a.question: What happens to tasks due today with no completion update?
D13a.answer: Ask 'Yes, I have completed it' / 'I have not completed it'; silence or elapsed time is not completion.

D13b.question: When and where is the completion prompt shown, how are other updates interpreted, and what follows 'I have not completed it'?

D14.question: When and where do advance reminders appear (timing, channel, repeats)?

D15a.question: Input mode?
D15a.answer: Available text and transcripts only (including local Wispr text); no live audio capture.

D15b.question: Where is a newly created task chat opened?

D16.question: Scheduling rules?
D16.answer: Use the owner's existing daily scheduling rules and protected time; ask for access if unavailable; never invent them.

D17.question: When does the review run?
D17.answer: Daily at 20:00 Asia/Kolkata, covering all agreed upcoming dates, not only tomorrow.

D18.question: What should the app do when a possible task, date, superseding agreement or task identity is unclear?

D19a.question: What if a task has no duration?
D19a.answer: Ask the owner; never estimate or default.

D19b.question: Prioritization, splitting and capacity conflicts when no permitted slot fits.

D20.question: Data handling: which histories are read initially, what is stored locally and for how long, and may transcript text be sent to the chosen model service?

D21.question: Operational exceptions: laptop asleep/offline at 20:00, task time already passed, input after the run, source/write failures, approval clicked after the batch.

D22.question: ChatGPT has no official automatable read path for consumer chat history (feasibility 2026-09-25). How should the required ChatGPT source be read?
D22.answer: ChatGPT stays the required primary source and evening processing must be automatic. Daily manual export, copy-paste, dropping ChatGPT and scraping are not approved; no workaround may be chosen without the owner.
open_parts: a supported automatic ChatGPT access route, or the owner's choice of the smallest change that makes one available
D22.notes: Verification 2026-09-25 (search-engine excerpts of help.openai.com and developers.openai.com; those domains were not fetchable from the build environment): no supported automatic read of consumer (Plus/Pro) ChatGPT conversations was found. The OpenAI API cannot read chatgpt.com chats; self-service export is manual (up to 7 days, link expires after 24 h); apps/MCP connectors receive only what a live chat sends and must not request chat history; the macOS app encrypts its local store. Supported routes with limits: (1) the Compliance Platform delivers conversation logs for ChatGPT Enterprise and Edu workspaces only (sales-led, org-level); (2) a ChatGPT scheduled task can deliver a daily result by push or email, but whether a task sees chat history is unverified and output would be a summary, not transcripts. Requirement R2 stays BLOCKED.

D23.question: Which runtime AI performs extraction inside the planner, within existing subscriptions?
D23.notes: Candidates found: Codex CLI signed in with the ChatGPT plan, Claude Code headless mode with the Claude plan (without --bare), or a local model. Each shares plan quotas or has quality/hardware limits; none is verified on the owner's laptop.

D25.question: Spending constraint?
D25.answer: Use existing subscriptions; no additional API or GPU spending without asking.
D25.source: owner interview 2026-09-25 interview constraints IST (private handoff; paraphrased)

D26.question: Google OAuth app mode for a personal unattended app: 'Testing' (refresh tokens expire every 7 days, requiring weekly re-consent) or 'In production' unverified personal use (one-time warning screen)?

R1.statement: Run the daily review at 20:00 Asia/Kolkata.

R2.statement: Read available work conversations and transcripts: ChatGPT required and primary, Claude optional, requested local Wispr text and other authorized sources after access is verified.

R4.statement: Infer tasks from discussions and follow the latest agreed state; a quoted old plan does not restore it.

R5.statement: The evening review processes new tasks across all agreed upcoming dates, not only tomorrow.

R6.statement: Place tasks using the existing daily scheduling rules and protected time; ask for schedule access if unavailable.

R7.statement: If a task has no duration, ask the owner; never estimate or default.

R8.statement: Create new Google Calendar entries automatically during the evening run when information and scheduling rules are settled.

R9.statement: Changes to existing calendar entries require approval through a clickable pop-up.

R10.statement: Reprocessing the same obligation never creates a duplicate calendar event.

R11.statement: For tasks due today without a completion update, ask 'Yes, I have completed it' / 'I have not completed it'; silence is not completion.

R13.statement: Use existing subscriptions; no additional API or GPU spending without asking.

R14.statement: Success criteria and release acceptance for the planner.

R15.statement: Behaviour when the 20:00 run is missed or an operation fails.

R17.statement: Fresh generation of the planner by PEOS is proven by retained evidence.
